A1.justification: Both PDFs contain complete, readable versions of the same 3D-MOOD work, including corresponding equations, Tables 1–10, Figures 1–8, and Appendices A–H. Textual and visual inspection supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D-MOOD benchmark experiments, cross-domain evaluations, ablations, and appendix results on ScanNet200, depth accuracy, memory consumption, and inference speed.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and ScanNet200 results in Table 8.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.7 retain the same lifting head, canonical image space, auxiliary depth head, geometry-aware queries, gradient detachment, and training losses. Figure 2's visual adjustments do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Omni3D datasets, Argoverse 2, ScanNet and ScanNet200, KITTI depth evaluation, and in-the-wild examples. Open-set, closed-set, and cross-domain task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: Cube R-CNN variants, OVM3D-Det, Uni-MODE, the other Omni3D baselines, and appendix depth comparators remain. The qualitative Gemini 2 comparison is also retained.

E3.justification: Training schedules, batch sizes, image resolution, augmentation, dataset splits and sampling, cross-domain evaluation design, and AP/ODS metrics are unchanged. Both retain 120-epoch main training and 12-epoch ablations.

E4.justification: The component ablations, padding/memory comparison, virtual-depth comparison, backbone ablation, matching-criterion analyses, and qualitative case studies are retained without substantive revision (Tables 4–6, 9–10 and Figures 4–8).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability, or significance tests. The reporting of point estimates and metric aggregation is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Swin-B ODS remains 23.8 on Argoverse 2 and 31.5 on ScanNet (Table 1), and 12.4 on ScanNet200 (Table 8).

T1.justification: The problem formulation, bounding-box parameterization, Equations 1–6, and normalized matching/error definitions in Appendix G are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first end-to-end monocular open-set 3D detector, the same lifting and geometry-aware contributions, an open-set benchmark, and state-of-the-art results. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations for generalization, limited auxiliary-depth benefits, and virtual-depth convergence behavior. Appendix discussions of depth accuracy, backbone effects, and metric suitability add no new interpretations or limitations in v2.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, preprocessing instructions, hardware and runtime information, visualization thresholds, and code/model access information are unchanged. The Vis4D bibliography correction does not alter the documented software or resource access.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 67 works and retain the same research positioning. Vis4D moves from reference 59 to 56 after author-formatting and capitalization corrections; associated renumbering does not change the cited research.

P1.justification: v2 expands the affiliation from INSAIT to INSAIT, Sofia University, changes the acknowledgment heading, and cleans up the Vis4D bibliography entry. The scientific prose and main-text/appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 slightly reformats Figure 2, adds printed page numbers, adjusts affiliation and acknowledgment/reference layout, and removes upward arrows from the Table 4 caption. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes limited affiliation, bibliographic, and visual edits while preserving the methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information throughout the appendices. These cosmetic adjustments do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall scientific quality or clarity.
